cohort: 69,672 women with singleton pregnancies delivering at 22-28 weeks of gestation whose infants were admitted to the intensive care unit
finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with increased odds of neonatal death, infant mortality (at 24 weeks gestation or later), and severe maternal morbidity in cephalic presentations, while in non-cephalic presentations, it was associated with decreased odds of neonatal and infant mortality.
mod_finding: In cephalic fetuses, cesarean delivery was associated with increased odds of neonatal death and infant mortality at 24 weeks of gestation and greater (not significant at 22-23 weeks) and severe maternal morbidity in all gestational age groups; in non-cephalic fetuses, cesarean delivery was associated with decreased odds of neonatal death and infant mortality in all gestational age groups.
